motion.name: --ease
motion.purpose: The easing for every transition and the view transitions.

motion.name: --fast
motion.purpose: Colour, background, border, ring and fade changes.

motion.name: --slow
motion.purpose: Movement: the nav underline, door fans, tile stacks, arrows, the phone buy bar sliding in.

motion.name: button-press
motion.purpose: Literal in shop.css: the face sinking onto its base (transform and box-shadow).

motion.name: scrub-crossfade
motion.purpose: Literal in shop.css: a hover-scrub slide fading in over the box art.

motion.name: scrub-rest
motion.purpose: In app.mjs: how long the pointer rests on a card before the hover scrub starts.

motion.name: pack-art
motion.purpose: Literal in shop.css: ::view-transition-group(pack-art), the card art morphing into the gallery stage and back.

motion.name: loading-dim
motion.purpose: Literal in shop.css: html.is-loading main, when a page takes longer than 120ms.

motion.name: intent-preload
motion.purpose: In app.mjs: mouse hover time on a link before its data and first images load.

motion.name: preload-wait
motion.purpose: In app.mjs: the longest a click waits for up to four images to decode before swapping the page.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Transitions and animations 1ms, scroll-behavior auto, view-transition animations off; app.mjs skips the morph and smooth scrolling.

motion.name: forced-colors
motion.purpose: Doors and department page heads keep their colours (forced-color-adjust: none); .btn, .chip and .top__lifetime gain a 1px ButtonText border.

narrative.overview:
The shop is Kash's thumbnail livery turned into a store. The box art he makes for every pack already carries the brand: a charcoal ground, an orange diagonal band for model packs, marketing blue for UI packs, a black skewed label strip and Montserrat Black lettering. The interface is built from the same few materials so that it never competes with the art. Box art is shown at full size with nothing around it, and the chrome is flat charcoal with one accent colour at a time.

The site is dark because its visitors work in Roblox Studio's dark theme. Density is that of a real storefront: four box arts across on a desktop, two on a phone, separated by generous gaps instead of borders. The home page is split by one diagonal into two departments, the orange Model packs door and the blue UI packs door, and the department's colour follows the visitor into its catalog and pack pages. Words are few and short. Weight and size carry the hierarchy, not extra lines of text.

Motion is quick and has a job. Moving between shop pages never reloads the page; the clicked card's art morphs into the pack gallery, and a pointer that rests on a card scrubs through the pack's slides. Everything that moves stops under reduced motion. The direction for this shop refused a gradient headline over equal tile cards on grid paper.
keyCharacteristics: A baseplate charcoal ground (#1A1C20) with flat tonal steps above and below it, and no grid lines.
One accent per department: livery orange for model packs and marketing blue (#49BAEC) for UI packs, always with dark ink on top.
Montserrat only: 900 for names, 800 for card names and buttons.
Product cards with no container: the 1:1 box art is the card.
Buttons whose face sits on a 2px darker base and sinks onto it when pressed.
Hard diagonals (the stage seam, the page-head edge, the label strip, skewed marks) instead of soft gradients.

rules.name: The Two Doors Rule
rules.body: Orange means model packs and blue means UI packs. A component takes its colour through `--accent`, so `data-dept="ui"` is the only switch. Only shop-wide pieces (the Lifetime Pack, the newsletter button, the plugin livery) name orange directly.

rules.name: The Dark Ink Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on an orange or blue field are always Dark Ink (#121316), which holds 8.75:1 on orange and 8.42:1 on blue. White on orange is 2.12:1 and is never used.

rules.name: The One Step Up Rule
rules.body: Hover moves a charcoal surface one step up the ladder: raised becomes raised-2, and a neutral button face becomes #343941. An accent surface on hover mixes 12% white into the accent instead.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Montserrat is the only typeface. Weight carries the hierarchy: 900 for names and prices, 800 for card names, buttons and labels, 700 for navigation, chips and counts, 600 for meta, 500 for body text.

rules.name: The Say It Once Rule
rules.body: A card or a row says each thing once: the name, one meta line, the price. Kash's rule for every screen applies: "Cut taglines, helper text and secondary labels. If a screen needs them to make sense, fix the layout."

rules.name: The Flat Ladder Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces are flat. A shadow belongs only to something that floats over content (the dropdown, the fanned art) or that is pressed (the button base).

rules.name: The Ground Gap Rule
rules.body: A ring around art is the accent separated from the art by a band of ground colour, never an accent border touching the image.

rules.name: The Six Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every surface uses the 6px radius. The smaller 4px radius is only for small pieces such as search rows and gallery thumbnails, and there are no pills.

rules.name: The Hard Diagonal Rule
rules.body: Diagonals are cut with clip-path, skew or hard-stop gradients, never blended. The only soft gradients in the shop are fade masks at the edge of a sideways-scrolling row.

rules.name: The Art Is The Card Rule
rules.body: A product, collection or plugin is shown by its art at full size with its name under it. Nothing frames the art, and every state (hover, focus, selected, scrubbing) happens on or around the art itself.

dos: Do take every colour from the `:root` tokens, and switch department only with `data-dept="ui"`; components ask for `--accent` and `--accent-base`, and only shop-wide pieces (the Lifetime Pack, the newsletter button, the plugin livery) name orange directly.
Do set text on Livery Orange (#FF9A1F) and Marketing Blue (#49BAEC) in Dark Ink (#121316).
Do show box art square and at full size with the 6px radius and nothing around it, with the name, one meta line and the price under it.
Do give every button its face on a 2px darker base (`box-shadow: 0 2px 0 var(--base)`) and let the face sink 2px when pressed.
Do mark hover and focus on art with the ground-gap ring (`0 0 0 3px var(--ground), 0 0 0 5px var(--accent)`), and keep the 2px accent focus outline on every control.
Do move a charcoal surface one step up the ladder on hover (raised to raised-2).
Do time motion with `--fast` (160ms) or `--slow` (420ms) on `--ease`, and turn it off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do use tabular numerals for prices and counts.
Do keep one search box, in the header: it filters a catalog page in place and suggests packs everywhere else.
donts: Don't add taglines, helper text or secondary labels. Kash: "Cut taglines, helper text and secondary labels. If a screen needs them to make sense, fix the layout."
Don't put white text on orange or blue; white on orange is 2.12:1.
Don't use any blue other than Marketing Blue (#49BAEC) for UI packs.
Don't wrap a product card in a panel, border, background or padding.
Don't add a second typeface, a system display face or a monospace face.
Don't blend colours in a gradient or draw grid lines on the ground; cut diagonals as hard edges.
Don't put a resting shadow under a flat surface; shadows belong to the button base and to things that float over content.
Don't use a radius other than 6px, apart from 4px on small pieces such as search rows and gallery thumbnails.
Don't add new hard-coded colours; reuse a token, or add one to `:root` and to this file.
Don't use the legacy aliases (`--panel`, `--line`, `--text`, `--gold`) in new shop CSS.
